corners.name: T1
corners.tip: Carry momentum: brake lightly or just lift, use one smooth steering input, and let the car run to the outside on exit. Over-slowing here costs a lot.

corners.name: T2
corners.tip: Slow in, fast out: do all your braking in a straight line, turn in late, apex late, then get to full throttle as early as the exit allows.

corners.name: T3
corners.tip: Trail brake toward the apex, aim for a slightly late apex, and use all the road on exit so you can open the steering and throttle early.

setup.title: Understeer on corner entry
setup.detail: Try trail braking deeper first (a driving fix). Setup options: move brake bias 1% rearward, soften front bump/rebound damping, or soften the front bar.

setup.title: Oversteer on power (exit) in 2 corners
setup.detail: Rear steps out on throttle. Try: TC one step higher, softer rear anti-roll bar, less diff power lock, or 0.5 psi less rear pressure. Driving fix: more progressive throttle.

setup.title: Front wheels locking
setup.detail: Move brake bias 1-2% rearward (telemetry reads 46%; check the garage value), or reduce brake pressure slightly.

setup.title: FL: inside only 1.9°C hotter than outside
setup.detail: Not enough negative camber; the outside edge is working too hard. Add about 0.2-0.3° negative camber.

pros.title: Clean, repeatable lines through T3, T5
pros.detail: You hit the same apex as your best lap with no mid-corner corrections. That consistency is what lets you push braking points later.

pros.title: You commit to the brake pedal in 3 of 4 braking zones
pros.detail: You hit 90-100% brake pressure in T1, T2, T3. Many newer drivers never press hard enough; you do, and that's the foundation of late braking.

pros.title: Fast, decisive brake application (T1, T2, T3)
pros.detail: You reach peak pressure in under 0.2 s. That is exactly right: the first part of the braking zone is where the tyres have the most grip.

pros.title: You get back on the throttle at the slowest point in 5 corners
pros.detail: Picking up the throttle at the apex (not after it) is good timing. The problem is what happens just before that point; see weaknesses.

pros.title: 68.7% of the lap at full throttle
pros.detail: Strong commitment on the straights and exits for this track.

pros.title: Your fastest passes through T5 were slower at the apex
pros.detail: That's "slow in, fast out" working: giving up a little apex speed for a better exit. Do it every lap in these corners.

cons.title: Coasting: 13.2% of the lap with neither pedal pressed
cons.detail: About 119 m per lap in T2, T3, T4. You come off the brake, roll, and only then pick up the throttle. The car is slowing with nothing controlling its balance, so you lose time and the front goes light before the apex.

cons.title: Braking into ABS in 3 corners
cons.detail: In T1, T2, T3 ABS is active for 72% of the zone at worst. ABS is a safety net; leaning on it lengthens your stops and hides where the real limit is.

cons.title: Rear wheelspin on exit in 3 corners
cons.detail: T2, T3, T5. Your rear tyres run 9°C hotter than the fronts, which is a symptom. Spinning wheels don't accelerate the car; they just cook the tyres.

cons.title: Slow to build brake pressure (T5)
cons.detail: It takes you 0.49 s to reach peak. Aim for 0.1-0.2 s.

cons.title: Brake released abruptly while turning (T2)
cons.detail: Snapping off the brake mid-turn-in unloads the front tyres and causes understeer at the apex.

cons.title: Wheels locking (T1)
cons.detail: Locked wheels don't steer and flat-spot the tyre.

cons.title: Busy hands: steering corrections mid-corner (T1, T2)
cons.detail: Repeated small corrections mean the car is moving around under you or the line needs adjusting mid-corner. Both cost speed.

cons.title: Not using all the road on exit (T1, T2, T4, T5)
cons.detail: T1: about 4.5 m more was available; T2: about 1.5 m more was available; T4: about 1.8 m more was available; T5: about 4.6 m more was available. Using the full width lets you straighten the wheel and get on the throttle sooner.

cons.title: Inconsistent through T3, T2, T5, T4, T1
cons.detail: T3: 0.90 s between your average and best pass; T2: 0.53 s between your average and best pass; T5: 0.31 s between your average and best pass; T4: 0.24 s between your average and best pass; T1: 0.17 s between your average and best pass.

improve.title: Connect the brake to the throttle
improve.target: Coasting under 8% of the lap, and under 10 m in any corner
improve.how: Keep 10-20% brake on as you turn in and hold it until the slowest point, then go straight to a light throttle. No gap between the pedals. Practice only this for 5 laps, starting with T4, T3.

improve.title: Threshold braking: hard first, then bleed off
improve.target: ABS active less than 20% of each braking zone
improve.how: Hit 90-100% immediately at high speed, then progressively release as the car slows. A formula car loses downforce as it slows, so the same pedal pressure that was fine at 280 km/h locks the wheels at 120 km/h.

improve.title: Squeeze the throttle on exits
improve.target: Rear tyres within ~10°C of the fronts; no wheelspin flags
improve.how: In slow corners take about a second to go from 0 to 100% throttle, and only go to full once the steering is unwinding. Short-shift (change up early) out of hairpins. Consider turning traction control on while you learn.

improve.title: Use all the road on exit
improve.target: Let the car run out to the edge on every exit
improve.how: In T1, T2, T4, T5, aim to finish the corner right at the outside edge. If you're not getting there, you're probably apexing too late or lifting; commit to the throttle and let the car drift out.

stopDoing.title: Letting go of both pedals between braking and the apex
stopDoing.detail: Every metre without a pedal is time you are not using.

stopDoing.title: Holding the brake pedal flat and letting ABS do the work
stopDoing.detail: Ease off as soon as you feel ABS chatter or see the ABS light.

stopDoing.title: Going to full throttle while the car is still turning
stopDoing.detail: Add throttle as you take steering lock off, not before.

stopDoing.title: Snapping off the brake with the wheel turned
stopDoing.detail: Release it gradually over the last 20-30 m before the apex.

stopDoing.title: Keeping full brake pressure as speed drops
stopDoing.detail: Downforce falls as you slow; release pressure progressively.

stopDoing.title: Sawing at the wheel
stopDoing.detail: One smooth turn in, hold, one smooth unwind. If you need to correct, the input before it was too sudden or too early.

show.item: Live delta to your best lap
show.why: The single most useful number. It turns green/red within a corner, so you instantly know whether a change you just tried worked.
Keep these on while you fix coasting (13.2% now): you'll see the gap between the red and green bars. Remove once it's under 8%.
Your ES wheel already has RPM LEDs, so you don't need to look at the HUD for shifts. Keep the gear number visible.

show.item: Last lap and best lap times
show.why: Glance on the main straight only.
Cold formula tyres lock and spin easily. Check them on the out-lap and after a slide, on straights only.
Formula cars expect you to adjust these during a lap. Only look at them on straights.

hide.item: Full standings / timing tower in practice
hide.why: Irrelevant when you are learning. Use the relative (gap to cars around you) only in races.
Useful for your first laps on a new track. After that, learn the track by real reference points instead.
Never read numbers in a corner. Look through the corner to the apex and exit; read the HUD only on straights.
Only matter in long races. Hide them in practice to reduce clutter.

settings: Steering lock: formula cars use much less rotation than road or GT cars (roughly 360-540°). Let AMS2 set the soft lock for the car, and keep the in-game rotation matched to Pit House so the on-screen wheel turns exactly as far as yours.

Force feedback: high-downforce cars produce big forces in fast corners, so clipping is likely on a 5.5 Nm R5. Turn on AMS2's FFB HUD meter and lower in-game gain until the bar only touches the top briefly.
Keep damping and inertia low in Pit House (as in your R5-AMS2-Claude preset). Formula steering should feel quick and light at low speed.
Learn with brake bias slightly rearward of where it locks the fronts, and ABS/TC on if the car allows it; turn them off later.
